0: My Hero Academia by Kohei Horikoshi (Viz Media) is a big-hearted superhero action story. In a world where most people are born with a superpower called a Quirk, Izuku Midoriya is one of the few born without one, but he still dreams of becoming a hero. Then a chance meeting with All Might, the greatest hero of all, changes everything. It's full of school rivalries, training arcs and big battles, and it's a great pick for fans of classic shonen.
1: One-Punch Man by ONE and Yusuke Murata (Viz Media) is a superhero action comedy. Saitama trained so hard that he can now defeat any enemy with a single punch, and that's exactly his problem. Bored by fights that never challenge him, he joins the Hero Association, hoping to find an opponent worth the effort. Murata's detailed, explosive art pairs with deadpan humor, so it works for action fans and anyone who enjoys a good superhero parody.
2: Komi Can't Communicate by Tomohito Oda (Viz Media) is a gentle, funny school comedy. Shoko Komi is the most admired girl at her high school, but everyone mistakes her silence for elegance. Only her seatmate, Hitohito Tadano, realizes she has a crippling communication disorder and badly wants to make friends. He decides to help her reach her goal of 100 friends. The short chapters are sweet and quirky, perfect for anyone who likes cozy slice-of-life humor.
3: Jujutsu Kaisen by Gege Akutami (Viz Media) is a dark, fast-paced supernatural action series. High schooler Yuji Itadori has amazing physical strength but no interest in the occult, until a cursed object turns up at his school. To save his friends, he swallows a finger of Ryomen Sukuna, a powerful curse, and ends up sharing his body with it. That lands him at Jujutsu High, training to fight curses. It's a great fit for readers who like stylish fights and real stakes.
4: Naruto by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a classic ninja adventure. Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, lonely troublemaker in the Hidden Leaf Village, shunned for the fox spirit sealed inside him. He dreams of becoming Hokage, the village's strongest ninja, and proving everyone wrong. Placed on a team with the brilliant Sasuke and the clever Sakura, he starts taking on real missions. It's a story about friendship, rivalry and hard work that has hooked readers for two decades.
5: A Certain Magical Index by Kazuma Kamachi (Yen Press) is a science-meets-magic action series. Touma Kamijou is an unlucky student in Academy City, a city built around training psychic powers, and his right hand can cancel out any supernatural ability. One day he finds a young nun named Index hanging over his balcony. She has memorized 103,000 forbidden grimoires, and magicians are hunting her. Fans of big, sprawling worlds with plenty of characters will find a lot to dig into.
6: Golden Kamuy by Satoru Noda (Viz Media) is a historical adventure set in early 1900s Hokkaido. Saichi Sugimoto, a veteran of the Russo-Japanese War known as "Immortal Sugimoto," is panning for gold when he hears of a hidden fortune in Ainu gold. The map to it is tattooed on the bodies of escaped convicts. He teams up with Asirpa, a young Ainu hunter, to find it. It mixes survival, violence, humor and rich detail about Ainu culture and food.
7: Ai Yori Aoshi by Kou Fumizuki (Tokyopop) is a sweet, old-fashioned romantic comedy. Kaoru Hanabishi is a college student who walked away from his wealthy, overbearing family. One day a young woman in a kimono, Aoi Sakuraba, arrives in Tokyo looking for him. She was promised to Kaoru as a child and has loved him ever since. The two end up living together, keeping their relationship secret. It's a gentle, warm read for fans of classic romance.
8: Blue Exorcist by Kazue Kato (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series. Rin Okumura is a hot-tempered teenager raised by a priest, until he learns that he's actually the son of Satan. After tragedy strikes, Rin vows to fight back against his father. He enrolls at True Cross Academy to train as an exorcist alongside his twin brother, Yukio. It's a fun mix of school life, demon battles and family drama, with great character designs.
9: Fairy Tail by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a bright, energetic fantasy adventure. Lucy Heartfilia is a young celestial wizard who dreams of joining Fairy Tail, the most famous and rowdy wizards' guild in the kingdom. When she meets Natsu Dragneel, a fire-eating wizard searching for the dragon who raised him, he brings her into the guild. Their jobs turn into one big adventure after another. It's all about friendship, magic battles and found family.
10: Oshi no Ko by Aka Akasaka (Yen Press) is a gripping drama about the dark side of show business. Gorou is a small-town doctor and a devoted fan of the teen idol Ai Hoshino, until a strange twist of fate has him reborn as one of her secret twin children. As the twins grow up in the entertainment world, a tragedy sets them on very different paths. It's part mystery and part sharp look at idols, acting and online fame.
12: Rurouni Kenshin by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a samurai action story set in Meiji-era Japan. Himura Kenshin was once a legendary assassin known as Battosai, but he now wanders the country carrying a reverse-blade sword, having vowed never to kill again. When he meets Kaoru Kamiya, who runs a struggling sword school in Tokyo, he finds a place to stay. His past keeps catching up with him. It's a classic with great sword fights and a lot of heart.
15: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? On the Side: Sword Oratoria by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy action spin-off. It follows Aiz Wallenstein, the famous "Sword Princess" of the Loki Familia and one of the strongest adventurers in the city of Orario. While Bell Cranel's story plays out in the main series, Aiz and her familia take on their own expeditions deep in the Dungeon. Fans of the main series will enjoy seeing its world from the other side.
16: Rent-a-Girlfriend by Reiji Miyajima (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy full of awkward situations. After his girlfriend dumps him, college student Kazuya Kinoshita uses an app to rent a date. His rental girlfriend, Chizuru Mizuhara, seems perfect, but he soon finds out she's also his classmate and his next-door neighbor. When their families get the wrong idea, the two are stuck keeping up the act. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy messy, cringe-funny romance.
17: Love Hina by Ken Akamatsu (Tokyopop) is a classic harem romantic comedy. Keitaro Urashima has failed the Tokyo University entrance exam twice, but he's still determined to keep a childhood promise to a girl he can barely remember. When he goes to stay at his grandmother's inn, he discovers it's now an all-girls dormitory, and he's suddenly its new manager. It's a lively, slapstick-heavy romance that helped shape the genre.
18: Children of the Whales by Abi Umeda (Viz Media) is a beautiful, melancholy fantasy. Chakuro is the young archivist of the Mud Whale, a drifting island that sails an endless sea of sand. Most of its people have magical powers but are fated to die young. When the islanders find a mysterious girl named Lykos on a wrecked island, their quiet world is upended. It's a moving story with lovely art, for readers who enjoy thoughtful, bittersweet fantasy.
19: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End by Kanehito Yamada (Viz Media) is a quiet, thoughtful fantasy adventure. The elf mage Frieren helped a party of heroes defeat the Demon King, but for her, their ten-year journey was over in the blink of an eye. When her old friend Himmel passes away decades later, she realizes she never really got to know him. So she sets out on a new journey to understand people. It's gentle, funny and often moving.
20: One Piece by Eiichiro Oda (Viz Media) is a sweeping pirate adventure. Monkey D. Luffy ate a mysterious Devil Fruit as a boy and now has a body made of rubber. He sets out to sea with one goal: to find the legendary treasure called One Piece and become King of the Pirates. Along the way, he gathers a crew of misfits who become family. It's funny, heartfelt and packed with imaginative islands, perfect for anyone who loves a long adventure.
21: My Dress-Up Darling by Shinichi Fukuda (Square Enix) is a sweet, funny romantic comedy about cosplay. Wakana Gojo is a shy high schooler who dreams of crafting traditional hina dolls and keeps his hobby a secret. When the popular Marin Kitagawa finds him at the sewing machine, she asks him to make her a cosplay costume. Their teamwork soon grows into something more. It's warm and full of craft details, great for fans of cosplay and slow-burn romance.
22: Rin-ne by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted supernatural comedy. Ever since she vanished as a little girl, Sakura Mamiya has been able to see ghosts. In high school, she discovers that the boy who sits next to her, Rinne Rokudo, is part shinigami and spends his time guiding lost spirits. He's also completely broke. Sakura gets pulled into his ghost-hunting jobs. It's a fun, episodic read, great for fans of Takahashi's earlier comedies.
24: Attack on Titan by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) is an intense dark fantasy. Humanity lives behind enormous walls to hide from Titans, giants that devour people. When a colossal Titan breaks through the wall, young Eren Yeager watches his home fall and swears to wipe out every Titan. He joins the military with his friends Mikasa and Armin. The series is full of shocking twists and big questions about freedom and war, for readers who like gripping, mature stories.
25: Boruto: Naruto Next Generations by Ukyo Kodachi and Mikio Ikemoto (Viz Media) is a ninja action series that continues the story of Naruto. Boruto Uzumaki is the son of Naruto, now the Seventh Hokage, and he resents living in the shadow of a father who's too busy to spend time with him. As Boruto heads into the Chunin Exams with his own team, he must figure out what kind of ninja he wants to be. Naruto fans will enjoy the new generation.
26: The Quintessential Quintuplets by Negi Haruba (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy with a mystery at its heart. Futaro Uesugi is a poor but brilliant high school student who takes a high-paying tutoring job to help his family. His new students turn out to be the Nakano sisters, wealthy quintuplets who hate studying and don't want his help. From the start, we know he'll marry one of them, but which one? It's fun for anyone who likes guessing games and romance.
27: A.I. Love You by Ken Akamatsu (Tokyopop) is an early romantic comedy from the creator of Love Hina. Hitoshi Kobe is a high school student who's hopeless at everything except programming. He spends his time building artificial intelligence programs on his computer. One day, a strange accident brings one of them, a cheerful girl named Saati, out of the computer and into the real world. It's sweet, silly and very much of its era, great for fans of classic manga.
28: Dears by Peach-Pit (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi romantic comedy. When a spaceship full of aliens called Dears lands in Japan, the friendly visitors are allowed to stay and live among humans. High schooler Takeya Ikuhara wants nothing to do with them, until he rescues a Dear named Ren, who decides he is her master. Now Takeya must keep her out of trouble. It's a light, playful read from the creators of Rozen Maiden.
29: Dragon Ball Super by Akira Toriyama (Viz Media) is an action adventure that picks up after the defeat of Majin Buu. Goku is enjoying peaceful life on Earth when Beerus, the God of Destruction, wakes from a long sleep looking for a worthy opponent. That challenge opens the door to gods, other universes and stronger fighters than Goku has ever faced. It's full of big battles and the classic Dragon Ball humor, perfect for longtime fans.
30: The Promised Neverland by Kaiu Shirai (Viz Media) is a tense, clever thriller. Emma, Norman and Ray are the smartest children at Grace Field House, a loving orphanage run by their kind caretaker, Mom. They've never been allowed past the gate. One night, they discover the horrifying truth about what happens to the children who leave. Now they must plan an escape. It's a smart, suspenseful read for anyone who loves mind games and big reveals.
31: Silver Spoon by Hiromu Arakawa (Yen Press) is a warm, funny slice-of-life story from the creator of Fullmetal Alchemist. Burned out by pressure to succeed, city kid Yugo Hachiken enrolls at an agricultural high school in rural Hokkaido, expecting an easy ride. Instead, he faces early mornings, farm chores and classmates who already know their futures. It's down to earth and full of heart, for readers who enjoy coming-of-age stories.
32: As Miss Beelzebub Likes by Matoba (Yen Press) is a cute, gentle comedy set in Hell. Beelzebub is one of the most powerful rulers of the underworld, adored by everyone and secretly obsessed with soft, fluffy things. Her new aide, Mullin, is devoted to her and can barely handle how cute she is. Their workplace becomes a sweet, slow-moving romance. It's a cozy read with lots of fun demon characters, great for fans of light comedy.
33: The Saga of Tanya the Evil by Chika Tojo (Yen Press) is a dark military fantasy. A ruthless salaryman is killed and sent by a being calling itself God to be reborn as a little girl in a war-torn world. Now Tanya Degurechaff, she becomes a mage in the Empire's army, determined to survive and rise through the ranks. It's darkly funny and packed with battles and strategy, for readers who like morally gray leads.
34: Don't Toy with Me, Miss Nagatoro by Nanashi (Vertical) is a teasing romantic comedy. Naoto Hachioji is a shy, quiet second-year who spends his free time drawing in the art club room. When younger student Hayase Nagatoro stumbles across his manga, she starts teasing him mercilessly, and then keeps coming back. Little by little, both of them start to change. It's a fun, slow-burn romance for fans of high school comedies.
35: Mission: Yozakura Family by Hitsuji Gondaira (Viz Media) is an action comedy about a family of spies. Taiyo Asano is a shy teen whose only friend is his childhood friend Mutsumi Yozakura. It turns out she's the heir to a family of super spies, and her overprotective brothers want any guy near her gone. To stay safe, Taiyo marries her and joins the family business. It's a fun mix of action, family chaos and sweet romance.
37: Rainbow Days by Minami Mizuno (Viz Media) is a lighthearted romantic comedy about four high school boys. Natsuki Hashiba is a sweet, hopeless romantic who falls for a girl named Anna after a chance meeting on Christmas Eve. His three best friends, a playboy, an otaku and a quiet sadist, each have their own ideas about how he should win her over. It's a funny, warm look at friendship and first love from the boys' side.
38: Black Butler by Yana Toboso (Yen Press) is a gothic mystery set in Victorian England. Ciel Phantomhive is a young earl who serves as the Queen's "watchdog," handling London's darkest cases. His butler, Sebastian, can do absolutely anything, because he's a demon bound to Ciel by a contract. Together they take on murders, secret societies and the supernatural. It's stylish, darkly funny and great for fans of mystery and gothic drama.
39: Black Clover by Yuki Tabata (Viz Media) is a high-energy fantasy action series. In a kingdom where everyone can use magic, Asta is the one boy born without any. He and his rival, the gifted Yuno, both dream of becoming the Wizard King. When Asta receives a mysterious five-leaf grimoire that lets him cancel magic, he joins the Black Bulls, the rowdiest squad of Magic Knights. It's a fun pick for readers who love underdogs and big battles.
40: How Not to Summon a Demon Lord by Yukiya Murasaki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy for mature readers. Takuma Sakamoto is a gamer known online as the demon lord Diablo. When he's suddenly summoned into a world just like his favorite game, the two girls who called him try to bind him as their servant, but the spell backfires. Now he's stuck acting like a powerful demon lord. It's a fan-service-heavy isekai with plenty of humor.
42: Twin Star Exorcists by Yoshiaki Sukeno (Viz Media) is a supernatural action romance. Rokuro Enmado was once a gifted exorcist, but after a tragedy he swore off fighting the monsters called Kegare. Then he meets Benio Adashino, a stubborn girl exorcist, and learns the two of them are prophesied to be the Twin Star Exorcists, a couple whose child will be the strongest exorcist of all. It's a fun mix of battles, bickering and romance.
43: Cirque du Freak by Darren Shan (Yen Press) is a creepy horror adventure. Darren and his best friend Steve sneak into a mysterious freak show that has come to town. There, Darren sees a vampire, Mr. Crepsley, and an amazing performing spider he can't stop thinking about. One reckless choice later, Darren's ordinary life is gone for good. This manga version of the popular novels is dark and fast-paced, great for readers who like their horror with a coming-of-age story.
44: The Ancient Magus Bride by Kore Yamazaki (Seven Seas) is a gentle, dark fantasy. Chise Hatori is a lonely teenager with no family and no hope, so she sells herself at an auction. She's bought by Elias Ainsworth, a mysterious mage with a skull for a head, who tells her she'll be his apprentice and someday his bride. In his home in the English countryside, she discovers a world of magic and fairies. It's beautiful, thoughtful and quietly emotional.
45: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure. Bell Cranel is a rookie adventurer in Orario, a city built over a huge Dungeon, and he's the only member of the goddess Hestia's familia. When the famous swordswoman Aiz Wallenstein saves him from a monster, he falls for her instantly and decides to get stronger. It's a fun, upbeat dungeon crawler with a lot of heart.
46: Chronicles of an Aristocrat Reborn in Another World by Yashu (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy adventure. After an untimely death, a young man is reborn in a world of magic as Cain von Silford, the third son of a noble family. The gods, delighted with him, shower him with blessings, and he quickly grows ridiculously powerful. Now he just has to keep it a secret. It's an easygoing isekai for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and cheerful fun.
47: Bleach by Tite Kubo (Viz Media) is a stylish supernatural action series. Ichigo Kurosaki is a teenager who can see ghosts, but that's never been much more than a nuisance. Then he meets Rukia Kuchiki, a Soul Reaper who protects the living from evil spirits called Hollows. When she's injured protecting his family, she gives him her powers, and Ichigo becomes a Soul Reaper himself. It's known for its cool designs, sword fights and huge cast.
49: Jing: King of Bandits by Yuichi Kumakura (Tokyopop) is a whimsical fantasy adventure. Jing is a young thief whose skills are so legendary that people call him the King of Bandits. With his wisecracking albatross partner, Kir, he travels from one strange, dreamlike city to the next, stealing treasures no one else could. Each story is a mostly self-contained heist. It's playful and stylish, great for readers who like episodic adventure.
50: Goblin Slayer by Kumo Kagyu (Yen Press) is a gritty dark fantasy for mature readers. A young Priestess joins her very first adventuring party, but their simple goblin hunt goes horribly wrong. She's saved by a mysterious armored warrior known only as Goblin Slayer, who hunts goblins and nothing else. She decides to join him. It's violent and intense, so it's best for readers who want a harsher take on the adventurer fantasy.
51: Made in Abyss by Akihito Tsukushi (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy adventure. Riko is an orphan training to be a Cave Raider in a town built around the Abyss, a giant chasm full of strange creatures and relics. She dreams of following her legendary mother to its depths. One day, she finds Reg, a robot boy who looks human. When a message from her mother arrives, the two set out to descend. Its cute art hides an intense, sometimes disturbing story for older readers.
52: The Seven Deadly Sins: Four Knights of the Apocalypse by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure sequel to The Seven Deadly Sins. Percival is a cheerful boy who has spent his whole life on a remote mountain with his grandfather. When a knight shows up and turns his world upside down, Percival leaves home for the first time. He soon learns about a prophecy of four knights destined to destroy the world. It's full of action and fun new characters.
53: Tokyo Babylon by CLAMP (Yen Press) is a supernatural drama set in 1990s Tokyo. Subaru Sumeragi is a gentle teenage onmyoji, the head of a powerful clan of spiritual mediums, who takes on cases of curses and restless spirits. He's joined by his outgoing twin sister, Hokuto, and Seishiro, a kind veterinarian who claims he's in love with Subaru. It's moody and stylish, and this CLAMP Premium Collection edition is a great way to read it.
55: Blue Lock by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Yusuke Nomura (Kodansha) is an intense soccer drama. After Japan's loss at the World Cup, the soccer union starts Blue Lock, a training program that brings together 300 young strikers. Only one will become the country's ace striker, and the rest will never play for Japan again. Yoichi Isagi is one of the players invited. It's a high-stakes sports story with big egos, perfect for readers who love fierce competition.
57: Deadman Wonderland by Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou (Viz Media) is a violent horror action series. Ganta Igarashi is an ordinary middle schooler until a mysterious figure called the Red Man massacres his whole class. Framed for the killings, Ganta is sentenced to death at Deadman Wonderland, a prison run as an amusement park where inmates fight for their lives. It's dark, fast and bloody, best for older readers who like intense survival stories.
58: Elemental Gelade by Mayumi Azuma (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure. Coud Van Giruet is a young sky pirate who finds a girl named Ren sleeping inside a crate of stolen cargo. Ren is an Edel Raid, a living weapon who can fuse with a human partner, and many people want her. Coud promises to take her where she wants to go. It's a fun, fast-moving adventure with lively characters, though the English release didn't finish the series.
59: Love Me, Love Me Not by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a sweet shojo romance about friends who see love differently. Yuna is a shy, romantic dreamer waiting for her prince, while Akari, her new neighbor and classmate, is a practical realist. The two girls become best friends, even though they couldn't be more different. When Akari's stepbrother Rio and his friend Kazuomi come into the picture, their friendship is tested. It's heartfelt and relatable.
60: Accomplishments of the Duke's Daughter by Reia (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance with a smart lead. Iris is a duke's daughter who suddenly realizes she's been reborn as the villainess of a romance game, at the exact moment her prince fiancé breaks off their engagement. Sent away in disgrace to her family's lands, she uses modern knowledge to turn the struggling territory around. It's satisfying and clever, for readers who like capable heroines.
61: The Seven Deadly Sins by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) is a fantasy action adventure. The Seven Deadly Sins were once the kingdom's greatest knights, until they were framed for treason and scattered. Years later, Princess Elizabeth is searching for them to help save her kingdom. She finds Meliodas, the Sins' former leader, running a traveling tavern with his talking pig, Hawk. Together they set out to find the rest. It's full of battles, humor and heart.
62: Fruits Basket by Natsuki Takaya (Tokyopop) is a beloved shojo story about family and healing. Tohru Honda is a cheerful orphan living in a tent, until the mysterious Sohma family takes her in. She soon learns their secret: several members turn into animals of the Chinese zodiac when hugged by the opposite sex. As Tohru grows close to them, she learns about the pain the curse brings. It's funny, touching and an all-time classic.
63: My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected by Wataru Watari (Yen Press) is a sharp, funny high school comedy. Hachiman Hikigaya is a cynical loner who thinks the whole idea of a happy school life is a lie. After he turns in an essay mocking youth, his teacher forces him to join the Service Club with the brilliant, icy Yukino Yukinoshita. They start helping students with their problems. It's witty and surprisingly thoughtful about friendship.
64: Go! Go! Loser Ranger! by Negi Haruba (Kodansha) is a darkly funny action series. Every week, the Dragon Keepers, a team of beloved superheroes, defeat the Dusters, an evil army that is really just putting on a show. Fighter D, one of the Dusters' lowest grunts, is sick of losing on purpose. So he sets out to take down the heroes himself. It's a fun twist on the Super Sentai formula, great for readers who like underdogs and clever action.
65: Sekirei by Sakurako Gokurakuin (Yen Press) is a fan-service-heavy action comedy for mature readers. Minato Sahashi has failed his college entrance exams twice and is down on his luck. Then a girl named Musubi literally falls from the sky into his life. She's a Sekirei, one of 108 superpowered beings who must find a human partner and fight each other in a mysterious game. It's a lively mix of battles, romance and comedy.
67: The Remarried Empress by Alphatart (Ize Press) is a romantic fantasy drama. Navier is the perfect empress of the Eastern Empire, admired by everyone except, it seems, her husband. When Emperor Sovieshu brings home a runaway slave named Rashta and favors her openly, he eventually asks Navier for a divorce. She accepts, but with one request: to marry again, this time to Heinrey, the prince of the Western Kingdom. It's elegant and dramatic, for fans of court intrigue.
68: My Hero Academia: Vigilantes by Hideyuki Furuhashi (Viz Media) is a superhero spin-off of My Hero Academia. Koichi Haimawari is a college student with a weak, unimpressive Quirk who never made it into hero school. He still helps people around town in small ways, which is technically illegal without a hero license. When he teams up with an aspiring idol and a mysterious, aging vigilante, he gets drawn into the city's underground. Fans of the main series will love it.
69: Magi by Shinobu Ohtaka (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure inspired by the Arabian Nights. Aladdin is a cheerful young boy traveling with a flute that holds Ugo, a powerful djinn. When he meets Alibaba, a young man dreaming of riches, the two team up to conquer one of the mysterious dungeons that have appeared all over the world. It grows from fun adventure into a big story about kingdoms and fate, for readers who love world-building.
70: Kemono Jihen by Sho Aimoto (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action mystery. Detective Inugami comes to a rural village to look into a string of mysterious animal deaths. There he meets Kabane, a strange, quiet boy whom the villagers shun and call "Dorotabo." Kabane turns out to be half kemono, a creature from Japanese folklore. Inugami brings him to Tokyo to work at his detective agency. It's a fun mix of folklore, found family and monster action.
71: Radiant by Tony Valente (Viz Media) is a French-made fantasy adventure. Seth is a young sorcerer who lives in a world where monsters called Nemeses fall from the sky, and the few people who survive their touch gain magical powers. Determined to become a great Inquisitor hunter, Seth sets out to find the Radiant, the legendary source of the Nemeses, and destroy it. It's colorful, funny and energetic, great for fans of classic shonen.
73: Shaman King by Hiroyuki Takei (Viz Media) is a supernatural action adventure. Manta Oyamada takes a shortcut through a graveyard and meets Yoh Asakura, a laid-back transfer student who can see and talk to ghosts. Yoh is a shaman training to compete in the Shaman Fight, a tournament held every 500 years to choose the Shaman King. His partner is Amidamaru, the ghost of a legendary samurai. It's a fun classic with great battles and quirky characters.
74: Teasing Master Takagi-san by Soichiro Yamamoto (Yen Press) is a sweet middle school romantic comedy. Nishikata is constantly teased by Takagi-san, the girl who sits next to him, and he's determined to get her back just once. Every plan he makes falls apart, and he never seems to notice that she might like him. The short chapters are gentle and funny. It's a cozy read for anyone who enjoys light, wholesome romance.
75: Seraph of the End: Vampire Reign by Takaya Kagami (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action series. After a mysterious virus kills everyone over the age of 13, the world's surviving children are taken captive by vampires. Yuichiro Hyakuya manages to escape, but at a terrible cost. Four years later, he joins the Japanese Imperial Demon Army, determined to take revenge on the vampires. It's stylish and intense, for readers who enjoy dark action.
76: Days with My Stepsister by Yumika Kanade (Yen Press) is a quiet, slice-of-life romance. When Yuta Asamura's father remarries, Yuta suddenly gains a stepsister his own age: Saki Ayase, a beautiful girl from his school with a cool reputation. Both of them have seen their parents' marriages fall apart, so they agree to keep a careful, honest distance. Over time, their feelings slowly change. It's subtle and grounded, for fans of slow, realistic romance.
77: The Way of the Househusband by Kousuke Oono (Viz Media) is a deadpan comedy. Tatsu, known as "the Immortal Dragon," was once a legendary yakuza enforcer. Now he's left that life behind to become a full-time househusband to his career-focused wife, Miku. He takes cooking, cleaning and grocery sales just as seriously as he once took gang wars, and he still looks terrifying doing it. It's a funny, sweet read with short, easy chapters.
78: Call of the Night by Kotoyama (Viz Media) is a dreamy supernatural romance. Ko Yamori is a middle schooler who can't sleep and has quietly stopped going to school. One night, while wandering the empty streets, he meets Nazuna Nanakusa, a playful, strange girl who turns out to be a vampire. If he falls in love with her, he can become a vampire too. It's moody, funny and atmospheric, perfect for night owls and fans of offbeat romance.
79: Samurai Deeper Kyo by Akimine Kamijyo (Tokyopop) is a samurai action adventure. Four years after the battle of Sekigahara, Kyoshiro is a gentle, goofy traveling medicine seller, but he shares his body with Demon Eyes Kyo, a feared swordsman. When bounty hunter Yuya Shiina sets out to collect the reward on Kyo's head, she ends up traveling with them. It's packed with sword fights and colorful rivals, great for fans of classic action manga.
